clue.text: Splendid son — little learner taken out

indicators.note: says the learner's letter is removed from the word for little

parts.note: piffling means trivial, of little account
L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A boy is praised as splendid once a small pupil has been removed from the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' looks like it describes the learner, but it supplies a word meaning trivial, from which 'taken out' drops the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, jolly British word of approval meaning excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Old copper wearing blue material that puffs up in the heat

definitions.text: material that puffs up in the heat

indicators.note: the old copper is dressed in blue, so those letters sit inside the word for blue

parts.note: blue in the sense of risqué or pornographic
PC is a police constable, a copper

explanation.surface: A retired policeman in blue uniform is pictured beside some fabric that swells when heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts OPC inside PORN. 'Blue' is not the colour of a uniform but means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize kernels burst and swell when heated, a cryptic description of the snack.

clue.text: Solid privateer appearing in two areas creates mirage

parts.note: fat as a noun is a solid substance, as in cooking fat

indicators.note: the privateer's name shows up between the two area letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, given twice
Henry Morgan was a famous Welsh privateer

explanation.surface: A sturdy pirate turning up in two places at once produces an illusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Morgan was a 17th-century privateer licensed to raid Spanish ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a complex optical illusion seen over water, a kind of mirage.

clue.text: Mug — I had nothing to fill it

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes inside the word it

parts.note: O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone holding an empty cup confesses they had nothing to pour into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup; it is the definition, meaning a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is slang for a gullible person or fool, a synonym for a dimwit.

clue.text: Learned one tune that points up uncontrolled movement

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointing up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a song is a tune
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A scholar studies a tune whose shape signals erratic motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that points up' turns SONG into GNOS, a reversal in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gnostic is one claiming special spiritual knowledge, hence someone learned.

clue.text: Everyone in punt comes to Swan Lake?

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes inside the word for punt

parts.note: a punt is a bet, a gamble
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone in a flat-bottomed boat drifts to a lake full of swans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a boat on a river; here it means a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake is an example of a classical dance work, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Male in Sabbath-breaking who found lover in Troy

indicators.note: the male pronoun sits inside the rearranged letters
the letters of Sabbath are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man breaks the Sabbath, perhaps an ancient Greek who found romance at Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy is not the city but Sergeant Troy, lover of Bathsheba Everdene in Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd; 'breaking' is the anagram signal and 'in' places the male.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's heroine Bathsheba Everdene falls for the dashing Sergeant Frank Troy.

clue.text: Land sown with grass over in Michaelstow

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the letters are read upwards
the letters are found within the place name

explanation.surface: Fields in a Cornish village are seeded with grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds AEL inside Michaelstow; 'over' turns it round. Michaelstow is a village in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic or farming word for a meadow or grassland, often temporarily under grass.

clue.text: Book from oriental port about Zen mostly

indicators.note: the eastern port letters go round the shortened word

parts.note: E stands for east, oriental
Kiel is a German Baltic port

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A volume comes from an Eastern harbour and deals largely with Zen Buddhism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental' supplies only the compass letter, which joins the German port; 'mostly' trims Zen and 'about' wraps the port letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the books of the Old Testament, named after a major prophet.

clue.text: Slip article inside French one in market

parts.note: a slip is an underskirt

indicators.note: the English article goes into the French one

parts.note: one here means an article, and le is the French definite article
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An undergarment with an article tucked inside something French, on sale at a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'article', so 'French one' is LE. PETTICOAT LANE is a famous Sunday street market in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The street name is used for the well-known London clothes and bric-a-brac market held there.

clue.text: Presentation intended to reach China shortly

parts.note: a letter for you is one intended to reach you

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A talk is designed to get to China quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate. 'shortly' trims MATE to MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The format of something is its layout or the way it is presented.

clue.text: Satan with aim to create Devil's Island?

indicators.note: the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: The Devil sets out to make an island of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devil's Island' suggests the French penal colony; it is the home of the Tasmanian devil.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian island state is the native home of the marsupial known as the Tasmanian devil.

clue.text: Study always covers troublesome Horace account

indicators.note: the word for always wraps around the rest

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for always

indicators.note: the name is made unruly, its letters reordered

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
a log is a record or account

explanation.surface: A scholarly study keeps coming back to an unruly Horace's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troublesome' turns HORACE into RCHAEO; AY 'covers' it with LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline of studying the human past through excavated remains.

clue.text: Trojan woman with memory suffering

parts.note: and means together with
ROM is read-only memory in computing
an ache is pain or suffering

explanation.surface: A woman of Troy is haunted by painful memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector's wife in Homer and Euripides, one of the famous women of Troy.

clue.text: Greek physician nurses duke in West College

indicators.note: the physician's letters sit within the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West, the Hollywood actress

indicators.note: the physician holds the duke inside, as one nurses a child

parts.note: Galen was an ancient Greek physician

explanation.surface: An ancient doctor tends a nobleman in a college in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but Mae West. 'nurses' makes GDALEN, which goes 'in' MAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalene is a college of Cambridge University (Oxford's is spelt Magdalen).

clue.text: Pass note something that associates Cabbages with Kings?

definitions.text: something that associates Cabbages with Kings?

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Passing a note that links cabbages and kings, as in Lewis Carroll's walrus.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase echoes 'of cabbages and kings' from The Walrus and the Carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old word for cabbage, and Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme monarch, so it links both.

clue.text: Faustina regularly seen in vast region

indicators.note: taking every other letter at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A woman named Faustina is often spotted in a huge territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of Faustina.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent on Earth, a very big area of land.

clue.text: Weak plant taken outside lobby

indicators.note: the word for plant is placed around the word for lobby

parts.note: to sow is to plant seed
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A feeble houseplant is carried out of the entrance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to sow.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow can mean lacking depth or substance, hence weak or superficial.

clue.text: Abide With Me no hymn for this actress?

definitions.text: Abide With Me no hymn for this actress?

parts.words: Abide With Me no hymn for this actress?
parts.note: Abide With Me is a famous hymn; the Swedish film star famously said she wanted to be alone, so 'abide with me' would never be her anthem

explanation.surface: A well-loved hymn is declared unsuitable for a particular film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish screen legend is linked with the line 'I want to be alone', the opposite of asking someone to stay with her.

clue.text: Chaps gamble — neither begins to improve

indicators.note: neither word keeps its first letter

parts.note: men are chaps
to chance is to gamble

explanation.surface: Men taking a risk find that neither gets started on bettering things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither begins' removes M from MEN and C from CHANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise its quality, making it better.

clue.text: Attire worn by bishop?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: worn as in battered, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: Clothing that a bishop puts on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' is the anagram signal, and the whole clue also describes the hat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap worn by Catholic clergy, including bishops.

clue.text: Shell ready to devour an experimental facility

indicators.note: the money swallows up the other letters

parts.note: the ready is slang for cash
a is the indefinite article, same as an
a lab is a place for experiments

explanation.surface: A company is poised to take over a research lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd whose hard dried shell is used as a container.

clue.text: Something to sell that animal feeds on

indicators.note: the advertisement takes the animal in

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, used to sell things
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A sales item that some creature eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeds on' looks like one phrase; 'feeds' is the indicator and 'on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship, train or plane means being aboard it.

clue.text: Passage your compiler will read aloud

indicators.note: says it is the sound of the words that counts

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so I'll

explanation.surface: The setter will recite a passage of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or theatre.

clue.text: Neglect correspondence and abandon duty

definitions.meaning: desert a sentry station or job

explanation.surface: Someone lets the mail pile up and walks off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is both mail and a position of duty, so the phrase reads either way.

clue.text: Excellent reason to start with show

parts.note: A1 means first-class, read as AI

indicators.note: only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A great motive for launching a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (excellent) is written with the letter I standing for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: To air something is to display or broadcast it, a synonym for show.

clue.text: Turn aside from wife having cut benefit

indicators.note: the letter for wife cuts into the word for benefit

parts.note: to serve is to benefit

explanation.surface: A husband turns away from a wife who has slashed his benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer suddenly away from a straight path.

clue.text: Venery perhaps consuming mum in drama

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow the word for mum
the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
ma is mother, mum

explanation.surface: Hunting or lust, perhaps, absorbing a mother in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Venery means hunting or sexual indulgence, a misleading surface; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'consuming' puts mum inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is a medieval English morality play.
